clue.text: Behind operator's buggy, that woman's clutching tail of dog that hurts a notable curmudgeon

indicators.note: one thing placed behind another means the second piece follows the first in the answer

parts.note: on an American phone you dial O for the operator, so the operator's is O's
a buggy is a small cart

indicators.note: to clutch something is to hold it tightly, so one piece wraps around the other

parts.note: a pronoun for a woman already mentioned

indicators.note: the tail of a word is its final letter, so only the end of the next word is kept

parts.note: what you say when something hurts

explanation.surface: A cranky man whose cart has run over a woman's dog's tail.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's after woman stands for 'is': that woman is clutching the letter. Dialling O for the operator is a US phone convention.
explanation.definitionFit: Oscar the Grouch is the famously grumpy Sesame Street character who lives in a trash can, so he is a well-known curmudgeon.

clue.text: China removing limits for aquatic mammal

indicators.note: a word's limits are its two end letters, and removing them leaves only the inside

parts.note: china is fine ceramic ware, a kind of pottery

explanation.surface: The country China appears to be shedding its borders, with a river creature somehow involved.
explanation.walkthrough: China with a capital looks like the country, but it is the porcelain sense; 'removing limits' drops the P and Y at the ends of POTTERY.
explanation.definitionFit: An otter is a sleek fish-eating mammal that lives in and around rivers, so it is an aquatic mammal.

clue.text: One hundred fix a feeling of elation

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for one hundred
read the word as two symbols: f, the musical mark for forte, means loud, and IX is the Roman numeral nine

explanation.surface: A hundred doses of something, the craving of anyone chasing a high.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fix' is not a synonym here but a code to unpack letter by letter: F is the score marking for loud playing, and IX is nine in Roman numerals.
explanation.definitionFit: To be on cloud nine is an idiom for being blissfully happy, so the phrase names a state of euphoria.

clue.text: Polish a religious image in a historic river

parts.note: an icon is a sacred painting in the Orthodox churches

explanation.surface: Someone cleans a holy picture in an ancient river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Polish' is capitalised to suggest the nationality; it is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: The Rubicon is the stream Julius Caesar crossed in 49 BC, starting a civil war, so it is famous in history.

clue.text: Announce new Lear production in high definition

indicators.note: in says the reworked letters go inside the abbreviation
new means made over, so the letters are reworked into another order

parts.note: a production of King Lear is billed under the play's short title, Lear

explanation.surface: A broadcaster announces a fresh staging of King Lear, filmed in HD.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' rearranges LEAR into ERAL, which goes 'in' HD.
explanation.definitionFit: To proclaim or signal the coming of something, as a royal messenger once did.

clue.text: Composer improved her swing

indicators.note: something improved has been reworked, so the letters are put in a new order

explanation.surface: A songwriter helped a singer get her jazz rhythm right.
explanation.definitionFit: George Gershwin wrote Rhapsody in Blue and Porgy and Bess, and swing bands played his songs.

clue.text: Part of force, if regimented?

indicators.note: regimented means drilled into strict order, so the letters are marched into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Asking who would belong to an armed force once it is organised into regiments.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition, and its middle words are also the letters to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: An officer is a commissioned member of the military or the police, both of which are called forces.

clue.text: For example, Kafka in examination for auditors

indicators.note: auditors are listeners, so the word is given as it would be heard

explanation.surface: Kafka's work set as an exam text for accountants.
explanation.walkthrough: Auditors look like accountants inspecting the books; here they are simply people listening.
explanation.definitionFit: Franz Kafka was born in Prague and is the best-known writer from what is now the Czech Republic.

clue.text: Famous Argentine stunt: remix old joke

indicators.note: a remix reworks a recording, so the letters are put in a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A revolutionary's publicity stunt gets reworked into a tired gag.
explanation.definitionFit: A chestnut is a story or gag repeated so often it has become stale.

clue.text: Snatch money back, excluding $1,000 for software feature

indicators.note: going back means these words are read from the end to the start
to exclude something is to leave it out, so a piece is removed

parts.note: a grand, or G, is a thousand dollars

explanation.surface: A thief grabbing back cash but leaving a thousand dollars behind.
explanation.walkthrough: The G removed is the one the turnaround leaves at the very end.
explanation.definitionFit: A toolbar is the strip of buttons along the top of a program window, a standard element of software design.

clue.text: Update official with letter from Israel

indicators.note: with means one piece comes along beside another, so they are joined end to end

parts.note: a ref, short for referee, is a sports official
resh is a letter of the Hebrew alphabet

explanation.surface: A referee sends news with a letter from Israel.
explanation.definitionFit: To refresh a page or a list is to update it with the latest content, a synonym in computing use.

clue.text: Terrible cad and liar discussed Arab leader's fashionable embrace of left-wing causes

indicators.note: something terrible is in a bad state, so the letters of the words after it are jumbled
something discussed is spoken about, so we want a word that sounds like the next one

parts.note: a sheikh is an Arab leader, and the word can be said like a French word for stylish

explanation.surface: A scandal in which a nasty cad and liar talks about an Arab sheikh.
explanation.walkthrough: Sheikh has two pronunciations; the one rhyming with 'cheek' gives the fashion word.
explanation.definitionFit: Radical chic is Tom Wolfe's term for wealthy socialites taking up left-wing political causes as a fashion.

clue.text: Rush holds a sawbuck

parts.note: to hold something is to have it
a sawbuck is American slang for a ten-dollar bill

explanation.surface: A man named Rush is carrying a ten-dollar bill.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the wordplay as a sentence: it has ten. A sawbuck is a US ten-dollar note, from the X-shaped sawhorse that resembles the Roman ten.
explanation.definitionFit: To hasten is to hurry or go quickly, a direct synonym of rush as a verb.

clue.text: Customer's financial claim in court

indicators.note: one thing in another sits inside it, so a piece goes within the other

parts.note: CT is the standard abbreviation for court
a lien is a legal claim on property as security for a debt

explanation.surface: A shopper takes a money dispute to court.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for 'is', joining the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A client is someone who buys services from a business, so a customer.

clue.text: European raincoat is ragged

indicators.note: something ragged is torn and messy, so the letters are scattered

explanation.surface: A continental mac has seen better days.
explanation.definitionFit: A Croatian is a person from Croatia, a country in southeastern Europe.

clue.text: Jarring ringtone that's in the air

definitions.note: a descriptive phrase standing for the noun: something that is in the air

indicators.note: something jarring is jolted and shaken, so the letters are knocked out of order

explanation.surface: An annoying phone sound fills the room.
explanation.definitionFit: Nitrogen makes up about seventy-eight per cent of the atmosphere, the main gas we breathe.

clue.text: Frowning and somber over getting 100%

indicators.note: in a down answer one piece sitting over another comes before it

parts.note: to ace a test is to get every answer right

explanation.surface: Someone looks gloomy even after a perfect score.
explanation.definitionFit: Grimacing is twisting the face in displeasure or pain, much like scowling.

clue.text: Fans of rock band put on shirts

indicators.note: in a down answer, one piece put on another sits above it and comes first

parts.note: Devo was an American new wave band

explanation.surface: Concertgoers wearing their favourite group's merchandise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put on shirts' reads as getting dressed; it places the band above the shirts.
explanation.definitionFit: Devotees are enthusiastic followers of something, the same as fans.

clue.text: Outdid Johnny and Brian, returning about mid-January

indicators.note: about means around, so the reversed names surround the kept letter
returning means going back the way you came, so the names are read backwards

parts.note: Brian Eno, the musician and producer

indicators.note: mid points to the middle, so only the central letter of the month is kept

explanation.surface: Two celebrities were bested by someone coming back in mid-January.
explanation.walkthrough: The names are reversed together, and the middle letter of January sits between the two of them.
explanation.definitionFit: To one-up someone is to go one better than them, so to outdo them.

clue.text: Peter surrounds Hal with unknown soldiers in a line

indicators.note: with means one piece comes alongside the other, so it is added on
surrounding something means enclosing it, so the name wraps around the other piece

parts.note: Peter Pan, the boy who never grew up
x is the usual unknown in algebra

explanation.surface: Two men named Peter and Hal flanked by anonymous troops in formation.
explanation.walkthrough: Peter is a first name standing for a whole character name.
explanation.definitionFit: A phalanx is a close formation of infantry, originally in ancient Greece, packed shoulder to shoulder in ranks.

clue.text: Rob follows true believer

indicators.note: one piece following another comes after it in the answer

parts.note: T is short for true, as in true/false questions

explanation.surface: A man named Rob is a loyal follower of a true believer.
explanation.walkthrough: Rob is a noun here, a robbery, not a man's name.
explanation.definitionFit: A theist is someone who believes in a god, so a religious believer.

clue.text: No halos disturbed interstellar smuggler

indicators.note: something disturbed has been moved about, so the letters are out of place

explanation.surface: A rogue in space without any halo, troubled.
explanation.definitionFit: Han Solo is the Star Wars pilot of the Millennium Falcon, who began as a smuggler.

clue.text: Listen inappropriately, making no noise

indicators.note: something done inappropriately is done wrongly, so the letters go in the wrong order

explanation.surface: Eavesdropping without a sound.
explanation.definitionFit: Silent means producing no sound at all, a direct synonym of quiet.

clue.text: See 12
Honor Marilyn, displaying her first name

indicators.note: to display something is to show it openly, so the letters are on view within the words

explanation.surface: A tribute to Marilyn Monroe that reveals her real name.
explanation.definitionFit: Marilyn Monroe was born Norma Jeane Mortenson, so her original given name was Norma.

clue.text: Deranged pariah, alone with a musical instrument

indicators.note: something deranged is thrown into disorder, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A mad outcast sits alone with only an instrument for company.
explanation.walkthrough: This harp is one of the three Marx brothers in the long final across clue, missing its O.
explanation.definitionFit: An Aeolian harp is a stringed box played by the wind, named after Aeolus, the Greek god of winds.

clue.text: Assignment involves one postulate

indicators.note: to involve something is to take it in, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a post is a job or posting
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A homework task that depends on a single assumption.
explanation.walkthrough: Assignment suggests homework; here it is a posting to a job.
explanation.definitionFit: To posit is to put forward as a basis for argument, the same as to postulate.

clue.text: Beneficiary just articulated travel cost

indicators.note: articulated means spoken out, so the two words are heard rather than spelt

parts.note: an heir is a beneficiary of a will; fair means just

explanation.surface: Someone who stands to gain has merely spoken up about expenses.
explanation.walkthrough: HEIR FAIR said aloud sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: An airfare is the price of a plane ticket, a cost of travelling.

clue.text: Nonnative plants and animals coexist uneasily

indicators.note: something that sits uneasily is unsettled, so the letters do not stay in place

explanation.surface: Introduced species struggle to live alongside the native wildlife.
explanation.definitionFit: Exotics is the ecologist's word for species brought in from elsewhere rather than native to the area.

clue.text: Westbound streetcar, around six on Thursday, ought to produce an analytic system that might help you identify the loveless men at the end of three Across entries

definitions.text: an analytic system that might help you identify the loveless men at the end of three Across entries

indicators.note: one thing on another is attached to it, so the pieces are joined
in an across clue, heading west means moving right to left, so the letters run backwards
around means surrounding, so the vehicle wraps about the number

parts.note: TH is the abbreviation for Thursday

explanation.surface: A trolley ride on Thursday evening should yield a way to pick out the loveless men elsewhere in the grid.
explanation.walkthrough: The streetcar wraps around six before the whole thing runs westward. The loveless men are HARPO, CHICO and GROUCHO minus O (love): the ends of 24, 11 and 1 Across.
explanation.definitionFit: Marxist thought is a school of social analysis, and it also points to the Marx brothers, whose names end three across answers.
